blocks.prompt: 10. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\sec^2x\tan y\,dx + \sec^2y\tan x\,dy = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
Each term is (function of \(x\)) \(\times\) (function of \(y\)), so dividing by \(\tan x\tan y\) separates the variables.
Plan: divide, notice each numerator is the derivative of its denominator, integrate to logarithms, combine.
steps:
Given: \(\sec^2x\tan y\,dx + \sec^2y\tan x\,dy = 0\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: separable; divide every term by \(\tan x\tan y\), then use \(\int\frac{f'}{f} = \ln|f|\).

Separate the variables
\[\dfrac{\sec^2x}{\tan x}\,dx + \dfrac{\sec^2y}{\tan y}\,dy = 0\]
Why: dividing by \(\tan x\tan y\) leaves only \(x\) in the first term and only \(y\) in the second.

Integrate
\[\ln|\tan x| + \ln|\tan y| = \ln|C|\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{dx}\tan x = \sec^2x\), so \(\int\frac{\sec^2x}{\tan x}\,dx = \ln|\tan x|\); the same for \(y\). Constant written as \(\ln|C|\).

Combine and remove the logs
\[\ln|\tan x\tan y| = \ln|C|\]
\[\tan x\tan y = C\]
Why: \(\ln a + \ln b = \ln ab\); equal logs give equal arguments (sign absorbed in \(C\)).

Check
Differentiate \(\tan x\tan y = C\):
\[\sec^2x\tan y + \tan x\sec^2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0\]
Multiply by \(dx\): \(\sec^2x\tan y\,dx + \sec^2y\tan x\,dy = 0\), the given equation.
